quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that best develops the topic sentence.
quests.prompt: Topic sentence: Carpooling makes the morning commute cheaper for workers.
options: Commuting can be a stressful part of the day for a great many workers.
Carpooling is becoming a popular idea in offices that have very large parking areas.
Sharing fuel and parking among four colleagues halves each person's weekly cost.
Some colleagues would rather listen to the radio by themselves while they drive.
quests.hint: The best supporting sentence explains or proves the exact idea in the topic sentence.
quests.explanation: This sentence shows how carpooling lowers cost. The other choices talk about popularity, radio or stress, which the topic sentence does not mention.

quests.instruction: Choose the best supporting sentence.
quests.prompt: Topic sentence: E-books are more convenient than printed books when travelling.
options: Many people like to read on trains, planes and buses when they go on holiday.
Some readers enjoy the smell and feel of paper pages when they read a novel.
One small device can hold hundreds of books, so nothing extra needs packing.
Printed books have a long history and are still sold in bookshops around the world.
quests.hint: Which sentence explains why e-books make travelling easier?
quests.explanation: This sentence explains the convenience directly. The others are about paper books, sensory preferences or reading habits.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO sentences that develop the topic sentence.
quests.prompt: Topic sentence: A weekly team lunch would improve morale.
options: Some restaurants offer a discount for large groups on weekdays.
People often feel more valued when a company invests time in them.
Lunch is usually served between noon and two o'clock in most offices.
Colleagues from different departments would get a relaxed chance to talk.
quests.hint: Choose sentences about how the lunch would affect people's feelings.
quests.explanation: Both correct answers link the lunch to morale. The others describe timing and prices, not the effect on staff.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that elaborates on the point by explaining it.
quests.prompt: Point: The new bus timetable is confusing.
options: Two routes now share the same number, so passengers cannot tell which one reaches the hospital.
Many passengers have said they are not happy with the timetable at all.
Timetables are usually printed on paper and displayed at stops along the route.
The timetable was published on the council website at the start of last week.
quests.hint: Elaboration answers 'How?' or 'In what way?'.
quests.explanation: The best sentence shows exactly how the timetable confuses people. The alternatives give publishing details or repeat the point.

quests.instruction: Choose the best elaboration.
quests.prompt: Point: Our website loads too slowly.
options: Pages can take over ten seconds to open on a phone, and many customers leave before seeing the prices.
The website was designed by a local agency around two years ago and has not been updated since.
Our website is a real problem for the people who visit it, and many of them complain about it.
Websites are used by customers to find information about companies, products and opening hours.
quests.hint: Which sentence adds detail about the problem, not about the website in general?
quests.explanation: The best sentence gives a measurable delay and its effect. The other choices describe websites, history or repeat the complaint.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that elaborates on the effect.
quests.prompt: Point: Working late has affected my studies.
options: Studies are an important part of student life for almost everybody.
I have a part-time job at a supermarket near the railway station in town.
Students in my year have many different kinds of jobs to pay their way.
I often arrive at lectures too tired to take notes, so I copy friends' notes before exams.
quests.hint: Show what actually changed in the writer's studies.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence shows how tiredness affects note-taking. The others describe the job, other students or general truths.

quests.instruction: Choose the best ending for the sentence that follows 'For example'.
quests.prompt: 'Public swimming lessons can build confidence. For example, ____'
options: a nervous nine-year-old at our local pool now dives in without holding the rail.
the pool is open from seven until nine o'clock on weekdays.
swimming is one of the most popular sports in the world today.
confidence is the belief that you can do something well.
quests.hint: 'For example' must be followed by a specific case.
quests.explanation: The correct ending is a specific case of confidence growing. The rest are general facts, opening times or a definition.

quests.instruction: Choose the best example.
quests.prompt: 'Simple house rules can prevent noise complaints in flats. For example, ____'
options: a 'quiet after ten' notice in our building stopped late-night arguments within a month.
rules are written by landlords and building committees each year.
many people live in flats in the large cities of the world.
flats are homes that share walls, floors and corridors with neighbours.
quests.hint: The example should show a rule leading to fewer complaints.
quests.explanation: The notice shows a rule solving a real problem. The remaining options define flats or describe who writes rules.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that does NOT work as an example.
quests.prompt: Point: Volunteering gives young people useful work skills.
options: One volunteer at the animal shelter now helps train new staff members.
A student who helped at a museum event later found work as a guide.
Volunteers are people who give their time without receiving any payment.
At the food bank, teenagers learn to manage stock and weekly schedules.
quests.hint: Three sentences describe real cases. One only defines a word.
quests.explanation: A definition doesn't show skills being gained. The other three are specific cases.

quests.instruction: Choose the topic sentence that keeps the paragraph on ONE point.
quests.prompt: Support in the paragraph: jackets cost half the price and shoes are often barely worn.
options: Second-hand clothes are good for the budget, the planet and personal style.
Clothes are an important part of daily life for most people everywhere.
Second-hand shops can be found in many towns and cities today.
Buying second-hand clothes is a good way to save money.
quests.hint: A controlling idea limits the paragraph to one main point.
quests.explanation: The best sentence matches the supporting details, which are all about price. One alternative names three points and the others are general.

quests.instruction: Choose the topic sentence that best controls the paragraph.
quests.prompt: The paragraph will discuss how night-time traffic noise affects sleep.
options: Sleep is important for health, and so is regular exercise.
Loud traffic at night can seriously damage people's sleep.
Traffic causes many problems for cities, including delays, pollution and accidents.
Some roads are busier than others at different times during the night.
quests.hint: Choose the sentence that names the exact effect the paragraph explores.
quests.explanation: This sentence names the cause and effect that the paragraph will explain. The others are too wide, too factual, or split into two topics.

quests.instruction: Choose the topic sentence that keeps the focus on cost.
quests.prompt: Support in the paragraph: refill ink costs a third of the price of new cartridges.
options: Printers are useful, colourful and fast for many tasks at home and in offices.
Refilling printer ink costs much less than buying new cartridges.
Refilling ink is better for the planet and for household budgets alike.
Ink cartridges are made from plastic, metal and a small amount of foam.
quests.hint: The details are about cost only, so the topic sentence should be too.
quests.explanation: This sentence focuses on price, as the details do. One alternative adds an environmental idea that the details don't cover.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the EXAMPLE?
quests.prompt: 'Team sports build friendships that last beyond the season. Players spend hours together in training and matches. Last year, our netball team held a bake sale and raised £300. Shared effort makes people trust each other.'
options: Team sports build friendships that last beyond the season.
Players spend hours together in training and matches.
Last year, our netball team held a bake sale and raised £300.
Shared effort makes people trust each other.
quests.hint: An example describes one particular event.
quests.explanation: The bake sale is a specific event. The other sentences make general statements.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the general supporting point (not the example)?
quests.prompt: 'Mentors help new employees settle in. They answer questions that manuals do not cover. My mentor once explained which forms the finance team actually reads. That saved me a week of guessing.'
options: Mentors help new employees settle in.
That saved me a week of guessing.
They answer questions that manuals do not cover.
My mentor once explained which forms the finance team actually reads.
quests.hint: The support is general, and the example is specific.
quests.explanation: The second sentence gives a general reason mentors help. The first is the main point, the third an example, and the last the result.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO sentences that are specific examples.
quests.prompt: 'Public art can make a neighbourhood feel cared for. A mural on Baker Street covered a wall that was often vandalised. The painted stairs near the station are now a popular photo spot. Residents say the area feels friendlier.'
options: A mural on Baker Street covered a wall that was often vandalised.
Residents say the area feels friendlier.
The painted stairs near the station are now a popular photo spot.
Public art can make a neighbourhood feel cared for.
quests.hint: Look for places and objects you could point to.
quests.explanation: The mural and the stairs are particular cases. The other two sentences are a general claim and a general result.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that continues the SAME point.
quests.prompt: 'Late-night deliveries are noisy. Vans often arrive after midnight. Their engines keep running while drivers unload.'
options: Drivers earn less than office workers in a number of similar cases.
Doors slam and trolleys rattle, waking people in nearby flats.
Online shopping has grown quickly over the past ten years in many countries.
Delivery companies also offer next-day service to most postcodes in the area.
quests.hint: The next sentence must add to the noise problem.
quests.explanation: The right sentence gives another source of the noise. The other choices move to service speeds, shopping trends and pay.

quests.instruction: Which sentence would BREAK the focus of the paragraph?
quests.prompt: 'Budget apps make it easier to control spending. They sort purchases into categories automatically. They send alerts before you reach a limit.' Which added sentence does not belong?
options: They show clear charts of weekly spending.
They can be set up in a few minutes.
They let users share a budget with a partner.
Some banks also charge fees for international transfers.
quests.hint: Three sentences describe features of budget apps.
quests.explanation: Bank fees are about banks, not about budget apps. The other three describe useful features of the apps.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that continues the argument.
quests.prompt: 'The Thursday meeting should move to Tuesday. Monday is full of deadlines, so people often arrive unprepared on Thursday because they are catching up.'
options: Tuesday avoids the Monday rush, so people can arrive ready to contribute.
The meeting room has a new projector that connects to most laptops.
Some staff prefer to work from home on Fridays and Mondays.
The weekly newsletter is usually sent out on the Thursday morning.
quests.hint: Return to the reason for moving the meeting.
quests.explanation: The right sentence gives another reason for the change. The alternatives mention equipment, newsletters or home-working days.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that best fills the gap.
quests.prompt: 'Cycling clubs help new riders feel safer. ____ For example, at my club, beginners always ride in the middle of the group.'
options: Experienced members show newcomers how to signal, brake and ride in groups.
Cycling clubs often hold their meetings once a month in local halls.
Some members race competitively, while others ride only for fun.
Bicycles were invented in the nineteenth century and have changed a great deal since.
quests.hint: The missing sentence should explain how clubs help, leading to the example.
quests.explanation: This sentence explains the help that the example illustrates. The others talk about history, meetings or types of members.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that fills the gap.
quests.prompt: 'Cafés should provide plug sockets at tables. ____ A café that added sockets last year now has a full room every afternoon.'
options: Some customers use tablets, while others bring only paper notebooks.
Many customers stay longer and spend more when they can charge their devices.
Cafés must follow safety rules when they install any new equipment.
Sockets are electrical outlets that supply power to devices such as phones.
quests.hint: Which sentence explains why sockets are good for the café?
quests.explanation: The correct sentence links sockets to customers staying and spending. The others define sockets, mention rules or describe customers.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that completes the reasoning.
quests.prompt: 'Staff should be told about rota changes at least two weeks ahead. ____ Last month, three colleagues had to cancel childcare at the last minute.'
options: Managers create the rota every four weeks for each department.
Rotas show which staff work in the mornings, afternoons or evenings.
Short notice makes it hard for people to arrange their lives around work.
Childcare can be expensive in many areas of the country.
quests.hint: The gap should explain why notice matters.
quests.explanation: This sentence gives the reason behind the claim and leads to the childcare example. The alternatives describe the rota or childcare costs.

quests.instruction: Which plan gives the best structure for a paragraph arguing for a school garden?
quests.prompt: Choose the plan that keeps the paragraph focused and developed.
options: Closing sentence → example: students plant seedlings → example: students water seedlings → topic sentence
Topic sentence: gardens teach practical skills → fact: soil has many layers → topic sentence repeated → closing sentence
Topic sentence: gardens teach practical skills → example: students plant and measure seedlings → explanation: they learn by doing → closing sentence
Example: students plant seedlings → example: students water seedlings → example: students pick vegetables → topic sentence
quests.hint: A developed paragraph usually moves from the main point to support, then explanation, then closing.
quests.explanation: The best plan states a point, shows an example, explains it and closes. The remaining options place the topic sentence last, add an off-topic fact, or begin with the ending.

quests.instruction: Which plan makes the most convincing paragraph?
quests.prompt: Topic sentence: Online forms save time.
options: Support 1: my own form took ten minutes → support 2: my brother's form took ten minutes → support 3: my friend's form took ten minutes
Support 1: no travel to the office → support 2: instant confirmation → closing
Support 1: the forms are colourful → support 2: some offices are old → closing
Support 1: they save paper → support 2: they help the environment → closing
quests.hint: Look for supports that stay on 'time' without repeating each other.
quests.explanation: This plan gives two different time-saving reasons. One plan drifts to paper and the environment, one repeats the same example and one is unrelated.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO supporting points that fit the topic sentence.
quests.prompt: Topic sentence: Coding clubs help beginners gain confidence.
options: Members can ask questions without worrying about looking silly.
Computers have become smaller and faster since the 1980s.
Some clubs meet in libraries and others meet in schools.
Small projects give quick wins that motivate learners.
quests.hint: Choose supports that explain how a club makes beginners feel more sure.
quests.explanation: Safe questions and quick wins support confidence. The history of computers and meeting places don't.

quests.instruction: Choose the sentence that explains why the evidence matters.
quests.prompt: Evidence: Twelve of the 30 desks in the study room have no power sockets.
options: Sockets are usually placed along walls or beneath the desks.
The room has thirty desks arranged in five rows facing the windows.
Students with laptops cannot work for long, so the room is used unequally.
The study room is open from eight in the morning until six.
quests.hint: Ask: what problem does this fact create for students?
quests.explanation: This sentence explains the effect on students. The others describe the room without explaining why the fact matters.

quests.instruction: Choose the best 'so what' sentence.
quests.prompt: Evidence: The clinic's phone line is open only from 9 to 11 in the morning.
options: Phone lines are used by clinics to receive calls from patients every day.
Two hours is a shorter length of time than a full working day.
That leaves working patients almost no chance to book an appointment.
The clinic has nurses and doctors who see patients in different rooms.
quests.hint: Which sentence tells us the consequence?
quests.explanation: The right sentence states the consequence for patients. The alternatives restate or describe.

quests.instruction: Which explanation goes beyond repeating the evidence?
quests.prompt: Evidence: During the trial, the shop's self-checkout was used by 70% of customers.
options: Most customers used the shop's self-checkout during the trial period.
The trial included many customers who came to buy groceries that week.
Seventy percent of customers used the self-checkout during the trial period.
The high share suggests shoppers value speed and are comfortable using the machines.
quests.hint: An explanation adds meaning; a repetition only changes the words.
quests.explanation: The best sentence interprets the figure. Two options restate it and one describes the trial customers.

quests.instruction: Put the sentences in the best order.
quests.prompt: Arrange the sentences about language exchange evenings.
options: Practising real conversations makes speaking feel less frightening.
At our monthly evening, a shy student ordered her first coffee in Spanish.
Language exchange evenings help learners speak more confidently.
Learners practise with native speakers instead of only reading from books.
quests.hint: The paragraph should move from the main idea to a closing explanation.
quests.explanation: The topic sentence opens, general support follows, then a specific example, and finally an explanation.

quests.instruction: Choose the best paragraph.
quests.prompt: Four paragraphs support the idea that community gardens bring neighbours together.
options: People who share a plot have to plan, water and harvest as a group. On our street, two families who had never spoken now swap vegetables every week. Shared work builds trust. Gardening is a popular hobby.

Community gardens bring neighbours together. People who share a plot have to plan, water and harvest as a group. On our street, two families who had never spoken now swap vegetables every week. Shared work builds trust.

Community gardens bring neighbours together. Vegetables can be grown from seeds, seedlings or small cuttings. On our street, two families who had never spoken now swap vegetables every week. Shared work builds trust.
Community gardens bring neighbours together. People who share a plot have to plan, water and harvest as a group. Neighbours also enjoy fresh vegetables at reasonable prices. Shared work builds trust.
quests.hint: The best paragraph keeps every sentence tied to neighbours coming together.
quests.explanation: This paragraph has a topic sentence, connected support, a real example and a closing explanation. Others drift to prices or growing methods, or lose the topic sentence.

quests.instruction: Choose the addition that would most improve the paragraph.
quests.prompt: 'Dog owners should keep pets on leads in the park. Last week, an unleashed dog ran into a children's picnic.' Which sentence should follow?
options: Dogs need a good amount of exercise each day to stay happy and healthy.
Parks have paths, benches and open grass areas for visitors to enjoy.
Some owners also like to walk their pets without any lead at all.
Children can be frightened or knocked over, and owners cannot always call a dog back in time.
quests.hint: The next sentence should explain why the example matters.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence explains the risk shown in the example. The others introduce exercise, park features or the opposing habit.
